recognize_zh: 紅血球之間兩顆無核小體，大小約紅血球的四分之一，中央紫色顆粒區、周邊淡染，形態一致，屬正常血小板。
features: Two small anucleate fragments roughly one quarter to one third the diameter of red cells
Central aggregate of purple azurophilic granules (granulomere)
Pale lavender peripheral hyalomere with smooth round to oval outline
No clumping, satellitism or giant forms
Background normocytic red cells, some slightly oval
describe_en: High-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows two platelets lying free between red cells. Each is round to oval, about one quarter to one third of a red cell diameter, with a central purple granulomere and a pale peripheral hyalomere. Granulation is normal, and there is no clumping or giant platelet formation. Findings are consistent with normal platelet morphology.

ddx.dx: Giant platelets (e.g. MYH9-related disorder, Bernard-Soulier syndrome)
ddx.vs: Giant platelets are as large as or larger than red cells, whereas these are about one quarter of a red cell diameter.

ddx.dx: Platelet lying over a red cell mimicking an intraerythrocytic parasite
ddx.vs: A platelet on top of a red cell shows a halo and granular texture without the ring cytoplasm and discrete chromatin dot of a Plasmodium trophozoite.
